summary: Amazon's Trainium 3 will be a materially better chip than Trainium 2, following the same multi-generation learning curve Google experienced with TPU.
summary_extended: Baker argues that Amazon's Trainium 3 will represent a materially significant improvement over Trainium 2, drawing a direct parallel to Google's TPU development trajectory where it took approximately three generations before the chip became a genuinely competitive and credible accelerator. He attributes this optimism to the Annapurna team at Amazon, which he describes as the most talented custom silicon team among all hyperscalers, suggesting the organizational capability is in place to execute on this generational leap. The investment implication is that Amazon's custom silicon roadmap is on a credible path to becoming a meaningful alternative to Nvidia's GPUs for training and inference workloads within AWS, which would reduce Amazon's dependence on third-party accelerators and improve cloud margin economics over the medium term. Baker uses moderate-confidence language ('probably a much better chip'), framing this as a directional view rather than a high-conviction near-term call.
detail: Baker notes the Annapurna team at Amazon is the most talented silicon team at any hyperscaler.
